A small first project

directories:

    path: _raw_data

proj --project . --non-interactive build-dev
The step-by-step example supplies the script, a tiny dataset, and the result to check. It uses Python’s standard library.

title: Preview release delivery
text:
The reviewed pipeline prepares a draft prerelease for an existing vX.Y.Z-preview.N tag whose version exactly matches Cargo.toml. It does not bump versions, push commits, publish an APT repository, sign credentials or publish the draft automatically. No new release is implied by this documentation.
Remote locked tests/builds produce Linux x86-64 and Windows x86-64 binaries. Linux uses Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35 or newer); the initial user-local WSL installation target is Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64. macOS/ARM delivery is not verified or supplied by this pipeline. Each asset is named proj_<version>_<os>_<arch>[.exe], with matching version.txt and checksums.txt. Exact-tag help/version/protocol smokes and actual installer tests must pass before assets enter the draft. Checksums detect corruption and mismatches; they are not independent signatures or reproducible-build attestations.
Installers default to MiguelRodo/projcli, require version metadata and exactly one matching SHA256 entry, and verify downloaded bytes before replacement. They stage on the installation filesystem and need only an existing user-writable directory. PROJ_RELEASE_VERSION pins a release (with optional v); preview releases should always be pinned because GitHub’s latest URL normally selects stable releases. PROJ_INSTALL_DIR selects an existing absolute user directory without changing PATH or system settings. Existing older releases lacking the new metadata fail closed instead of installing an unverified fallback binary.
Before publication: reconcile reviewed supported behavior and limits, update the Cargo/Cargo.lock preview version in a reviewed change, verify required checks, then create the exact reviewed tag. Inspect the resulting draft assets/version/ checksums and retain disposable-project warnings. Publish only after those checks. For WSL, download the pinned binary/manifest, verify SHA256, preserve any existing user-local binary, install into the chosen user-local directory and smoke help, version, capabilities and a disposable configured preview. No local compilation, sudo, persistent authentication change or R package modification is needed.
Known limits include bounded captured-state recovery, arbitrary external script effects, incomplete direct R/IDE parity, incomplete attempt/release records and analysis-free publication retry. This is a development preview, not M2 completion.
The prepared CLI package version is 0.4.0-preview.1; its review and the final integrated main checks precede creating tag v0.4.0-preview.1. Cargo.toml and the root proj entry in Cargo.lock match. proj --version and machine cli_version report that package version. proj version get reads an analysis project VERSION and is deliberately a separate value; existing project VERSION files are not bumped by preparing the CLI release. The feature status distinguishes implemented Rust behavior, pending recovery verification, R/IDE gaps and unfinished M2 records/provenance/retry. No broad milestone checkbox is closed merely to enable binary delivery.


0.4.0-preview.1 is published as a prerelease; stable Latest remains v0.3.0. Its tag workflow passed, and both uploaded binaries were downloaded, hash-checked and executed for help/version/capabilities. Public downloads matched the verified asset bytes. Source identity is bbd12edc8de9865a96b6145d0c7702f1300cb1a8; package version is 0.4.0-preview.1, protocol version 1. The WSL user-local install and disposable Python success/failure smokes passed without local compilation. See compatibility evidence.
Pin PROJ_RELEASE_VERSION=0.4.0-preview.1 when using the installer from that tag. Use an existing absolute user-local PROJ_INSTALL_DIR; installation changes no system/PATH settings. macOS/ARM artifacts remain unavailable. Keep the disposable- project limits and unfinished R/IDE/M2 scope from feature status.

title: proj path get
text:
Get the resolved absolute path for a given label in the project.
proj path get --label <LABEL> [--target final|safe] [--format auto|absolute|relative] [--relative-to BASE] [--project <PATH>] [PART ...]


A label must be declared in the active configuration with a nonempty path. ASCII case is ignored. Undeclared labels and suffixes are errors: declaring raw-data does not declare raw or raw-data-extra. Relative paths resolve against the captured project root; explicit external directories are allowed. Queries do not create directories. Final lookup returns the configured location; explicit safe lookup resolves the logical versioned-cache target.



--project PATH selects that exact existing directory, including a folder without configuration or VERSION. It overrides both ancestor discovery and an inherited run root. Invalid directories fail with a nonzero exit status.
The CLI captures an absolute root as PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT for the invocation and its child processes. A nested proj path get uses that root even after a script changes cwd. An invalid inherited root fails rather than falling back silently. Direct Rust build_project(root, ...) calls also pass their supplied root to children. See the discovery rules below for the recognized root markers.
This establishes CLI child-query behavior, not direct Quarto/RStudio parity or changes to the existing R frontend. Renderer configuration, execution cwd, resource links and output placement remain separate concerns. Path queries do not write ignore files or create the resolved target directories.



Without --project or an inherited run root, discovery walks upward from cwd and selects the first recognized directory. It does not search downward for projects. Recognized markers are VERSION, README.md, _quarto.yml, _proj.yml, legacy _projr.yml, Git/SVN metadata, a DESCRIPTION containing Package:, an RStudio .Rproj whose first line starts Version:, and a renv.lock with a Packages map.
pyproject.toml, Project.toml and JuliaProject.toml deliberately extend the projr marker set for Python/Julia. requirements.txt and Manifest.toml alone are not root markers. Standalone VERSION and README markers are retained, so a nested directory with one is the nearer project; explicit selection overrides it.
Marker recognition does not change shallow default script enumeration or prove that the corresponding language runner/frontend is implemented. Legacy config content handling is a separate compatibility change from recognizing its root.
If no recognized marker exists, discovery selects cwd. Discovery success does not mean a build is configured: the current product contract requires active root configuration and explicit used-directory mappings. Validation changes enforcing that newer contract are separate from this root-discovery slice.



--target safe maps declared output/data/docs-class labels to <selected-cache>/projr/v<active-version>/<exact-declared-label>. One explicit safe: true cache wins; otherwise eligible exact label cache wins, then the first eligible cache in merged declaration order. safe: false excludes a candidate. The chosen label is captured for child queries. A release version has no dev suffix; dev cache keys use a hyphen, such as v1.2.3-4. Other roles retain their configured targets.
--target final addresses the explicitly configured destination, including an absolute external directory. This intermediate slice retains final as the CLI default until build promotion is wired to safe logical output; that is a temporary compatibility boundary, not the final approved default path model.
Optional parts extend the selected role, for example:
proj path get --label output --target safe figures result.png
Queries do not create directories. Unknown labels, missing cache/version for safe lookup, absolute/drive-qualified parts and parent traversal fail clearly. Explicit directory mappings stay mandatory; output-model does not imply an output alias. Native cwd/auto-relative presentation and renderer staging are separate slices.



--format auto returns a caller-cwd-relative filesystem path in ordinary execution and an absolute target in an explicitly known managed render child. It never infers render context from a .qmd filename, project marker or cwd. absolute and relative override auto. Explicit --relative-to cwd|project|document|/absolute/base requires relative format; document requires an individually known render document. Project renders without a single document reject that base. A custom base must be absolute.
Strict relative conversion fails across roots/drives. Auto ordinary execution falls back to absolute when no relative path exists; the absolute target stays identical. The intermediate CLI still defaults to absolute/final until integrated consumers switch to the approved auto/safe defaults. Getters create no directories.
Renderer descriptors are private per-command snapshots created only when launching Quarto/rmarkdown/Bookdown, alongside unchanged root/profile/version/mapping inputs. Ordinary scripts and dependency probes keep ordinary context. Existing R helpers do not consume this descriptor; direct IDE rendering does not gain automatic parity. Absolute results are filesystem targets, not literal Markdown/LaTeX URL rewrites.

title: proj ignore
text:
Commands for interacting with tracking file exclusions, handling operations to manually or automatically modify .gitignore and .Rbuildignore files.


Manually appends one or more raw file or directory paths to the project ignore files.
Unlike automatic configurations driven by _proj.yml, these manual entries represent permanent, user-specified exclusions and are placed strictly above the # --- PROJ MANAGED --- blocks.



<PATHS>...: One or more raw file or directory paths to be ignored.
--force-create: Boolean flag (default true). If true, creates ignore files if they don’t exist. If false, skips file creation unless inherently warranted by environmental cues (e.g. finding a .git folder or a DESCRIPTION file).
--type: Optional filter selection (all [default], git, rbuild). Determines which tracking surface receives the manual path entries. Note that .Rbuildignore is skipped entirely if no DESCRIPTION file exists at the project root.





Manually forces paths to be tracked by appending negated syntax (e.g. !path/ or ^!pattern$).
These unignore entries represent permanent, user-specified negations and are placed strictly below the # --- END PROJ MANAGED --- boundary in .gitignore and .Rbuildignore files.



<PATHS>...: One or more raw file or directory paths to force tracking.
--type: Optional filter selection (all [default], git, rbuild). Determines which tracking surface receives the negated entries. Note that .Rbuildignore is skipped entirely if no DESCRIPTION file exists at the project root.





The library core automatically synchronizes ignore rules dynamically across .gitignore and .Rbuildignore based on the configuration of _proj.yml.

Note: While the automated ignore synchronization is invoked implicitly by the CLI via commands like proj yml read (and acts seamlessly under the hood), the ignore subcommand namespace exists openly to support explicit manual additions via proj ignore add.




The tool automatically locates the project boundaries via a heuristic upward path traversal. It begins checking from the user’s current working directory upward: - It discovers the conceptual root by finding a directory containing a VERSION file. - It continues upward through up to 5 directory levels seeking an optimal foundational root confirming the presence of either _proj.yml or a .git tracking context alongside the VERSION.



The tool targets specifically two core exception list files: - .gitignore (safeguards git commit environments) - .Rbuildignore (safeguards strict CRAN environments and rbuild processes)
Based on the individual block ignore settings within _proj.yml (e.g. ignore: all), properties are intelligently resolved as standard git glob patterns and Rbuild regex match patterns appropriately.



Modifications made by the tool into .gitignore and .Rbuildignore are safely strictly demarcated with protected slice logic block comments. This preserves user-defined modifications outside the managed span: - Operations scan for # --- PROJ MANAGED --- and # --- END PROJ MANAGED ---. - Targeted slice elements are swapped or appended into existing scopes only between these exact markers. - If the boundary blocks are absent, the tool automatically injects them natively at the base end.

title: proj version get
text:
Get the project version based on the VERSION file.


The command searches upwards from the current directory to discover the project root containing the VERSION file. It parses the version text (supporting both raw strings like v1.0.0 or JSON objects) and resolves it to a standard output.
If the VERSION file is missing, the tool attempts to fall back and parse the version from an R package DESCRIPTION file if one is present in the project root. If neither a VERSION file nor a DESCRIPTION file exists, it defaults to a newly initialized v0.0.1.
proj version get





Omits the ‘v’ prefix from the output string.
proj version get --no-v



Specifies the output format: - text (default): Outputs the version as a standard string identifier. - json: Outputs the version as a serialized JSON object, detailing its properties (major, minor, patch, and optionally dev).
proj version get --format json




When using --format=json, the output consists of the separated standard semantic components: - major (integer) - minor (integer) - patch (integer) - dev (integer, optional, indicating build cycles or pre-release versioning)

title: Future R wrapper: CLI installation and CRAN checks
text:
Status: design direction recorded on 2026-10-20, not a shipped wrapper or an accepted CRAN submission. The existing R package remains untouched. This note does not settle the complete frontend protocol or claim renderer parity.


The future wrapper is intended to contain R code that calls a separately installed proj CLI. Its DESCRIPTION should declare that CLI in SystemRequirements. It should discover a compatible executable and give an actionable missing/incompatible-CLI error. A user-invoked installer on the user’s own machine is distinct from automatic downloads during CRAN installation, checks or examples. Do not assume CRAN servers already provide proj.
CRAN source-package policy permits downloads of precompiled software only as a last resort with CRAN-team agreement. A separate executable is not an automatic exemption. Review Writing R Extensions: portability when implementing the package, including external software availability and portable invocation. This work has neither requested nor obtained CRAN agreement; no outreach is authorized here.










Environment
Required behavior




CRAN, CLI absent
Always run meaningful R-only validation, argument construction, missing-CLI diagnostics and mocked protocol/response tests. Skip only genuine executable integration tests, explicitly because the CLI is unavailable.


CRAN, compatible CLI available
Run the applicable real integration tests as well as the R-only tests. Do not assume every check host supplies it.


Our integration CI
Install an exact pinned CLI release, verify its checksum and compatible version, and run real end-to-end tests. Missing CLI or failed installation is a failure, never a silent skip.



Mocked responses check the wrapper contract; they do not prove the CLI or renderer works. Our mandatory integration job supplies that evidence. Examples and vignettes must also handle optional executable availability honestly instead of requiring an undeclared download. A requirement to execute proj on CRAN check servers would need an agreed deployment/checking arrangement, not an assumed policy exception.



The pinned Quarto R package DESCRIPTION at v1.5.1 declares the separate Quarto command-line tool in SystemRequirements. Its test helper can skip executable-dependent tests when Quarto is unavailable, and its vignette utility checks executable availability during vignette processing. These are specific implementation precedents, not proof that CRAN has accepted a future proj wrapper or guaranteed an executable on every server. This note does not infer automatic binary-download permission from Quarto’s existence.
Before implementation, specify compatible protocol versions, executable discovery, argument quoting, diagnostics, and which tests are unconditional versus executable integration. R production changes require separate authorization.

title: Preview feature status
text:
Preview feature status
This is an early Rust CLI for disposable analysis projects. A development preview does not mean the complete roadmap is finished. Use independent backups and sample data while evaluating it. The existing projr R package and thesis remain unchanged.



Area
Available Rust behavior
Verification and limits




Project selection
Explicit root; nearest recognized ancestor; markerless cwd fallback; shallow default script discovery.
Cross-platform fixtures cover markers, nested invocation and explicit override. Root recognition includes Python/Julia markers; that does not imply Julia execution or a wrapper.


Configuration and init
Active root YAML required; legacy alias/ambiguity rule; profile precedence; explicitly declared resource directories; local-only directory initialization.
Cross-platform configuration/error-preservation fixtures. Old no-config roadmap assumptions were superseded.


Execution context
Ordered explicit scripts/hooks; captured-root process cwd; supported Quarto/R Markdown root controls; unsafe/unknown layouts fail early.
Real Python execution and fake-renderer argument/artifact tests. Complete real R/renderer/IDE end-to-end parity has not been established.


Automation
Opt-in protocol-v1 JSON, capability version, typed queries, noninteractive command worker, nonzero failures; child logs on stderr.
Cross-platform machine tests. Static coarse error codes; no invented attempt/release record on success.


Preview preservation
This candidate restores captured managed state after successful/failed previews. Cache results remain.
Included through the reviewed recovery dependency; final integrated tests and actual released-binary checks passed. Not automatic output redirection or an OS sandbox.


Production safety groundwork
Path guards, bounded local failure recovery, optional checked Git publication and verified CAS bytes.
Focused fixtures and reviews; incomplete release identity/provenance/retry model. This page is not an invitation to run on valuable production data.


Binary delivery
Development prerelease 0.4.0-preview.1 supplies versioned Linux/Windows x86-64 assets with mandatory checksums.
Exact-tag workflow, uploaded/public asset hashes and both native binary smokes passed. WSL user-local installation and tiny success/failure Python previews passed. Other platforms are not supplied.



Still unfinished: direct projr/quarto R API/RStudio parity, existing R helper integration, full real R demo coverage, automatic isolation of every script write, durable attempt/release identifiers, complete input/code/config/dependency provenance, multi-writer/crash atomicity and analysis-free publication retry. Capture/recovery cannot undo arbitrary external script effects or guarantee concurrent readers never observe temporary changes. User/third-party logs are not automatically secret-redacted.
M1 and M2 remain open as broad milestones. Individual implemented slices are evidence toward acceptance; this status does not close or rewrite private roadmap checkboxes. See delivery boundaries, behavior and the compatibility log for supported details and remaining gaps.

The behavior contract owns current product decisions. This log records comparison evidence, implementation differences and gaps. Update it in every focused PR; do not infer runtime parity from similar source or green Rust CI.
Relationship labels are same, different, new, and unverified. Each entry states whether that label concerns documented intent, static source, or executed behavior. No comparative R runtime tests have been run for the entries below. Local R/Docker workloads have not been run.

Thesis baseline: design at b110da5.

New comparisons must pin source commits and relevant files, record the decision and rationale, link executed tests, and distinguish approved, implemented and unverified behavior. Changing a reference baseline does not silently change the product contract.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Same precedence / deliberate error handling difference: inherited OS values win over local, earlier environment profiles, then base assignments. Preserve non-Unicode inherited values rather than treating them as absent. Reject empty, equals-containing or NUL keys and NUL values before calling OS mutation APIs. Read whole files with propagated errors rather than lines().flatten(); required file errors and directory inputs cannot silently bypass validation or loop. Diagnostics include paths/line numbers, never assignment values. Same-file validation finishes before assignments from that file are applied. Ignore writes in explicit activation occur only after validation succeeds.
Ponytail full-mode review traced all load/assignment callers and reused existing configuration-entry presence checks. No parser dependency was added. Prepared CLI checks cover invalid/NUL entries, directory and permission-denied required files, secret-free diagnostics, actual inherited/local/profile/base child values and no analysis invocation on errors. Remote checks/review are pending.
This bounded fix does not make EnvGuard thread-safe: process-global environment mutation remains a known risk until per-run values and profiles reach all child commands and Git/preflight consumers. No credential handling or CAS code changes. ## Prepared managed-state restoration invariant (not yet verified)
The restoration implementation under preparation replaces the legacy middle-only catch and synthesized development-version rollback. Before controlled production mutations, capture exact bytes, permissions and absence for VERSION, ignore files, root configuration/state and existing root regular files; selected in-project inputs; declared output/docs directory trees; and concrete individual renderer output/asset paths. Capture initially absent parent directories too. Declared external output/docs paths are supported. Raw data, Git internals, arbitrary external user-script effects and cache contents are not backed up. Managed trees containing symlinks or unsupported entries are rejected rather than followed.
Backups use existing tempfile and streaming std::fs copies in private OS temporary recovery storage outside disposable project cache. No project mapping is invented, and cache-free upload-only operations remain supported. Recovery sources are copied to temporary restore staging before any current target is removed. Missing recovery bytes leave intact current state alone and are reported as unavailable.
One local failure boundary covers ignore synchronization, cleanup, all pre/both/ post hooks, engine configuration, execution, output promotion and VERSION writing. Promotion errors propagate; renderer configuration is restored byte-for-byte on success and failure. VERSION changes only after hooks/render/promotion succeed. Failures and caught panics restore captured state. All restore entries are attempted; if restoration fails, retain recovery bytes and report both the original failure and restoration failures with the backup path. Substituted links are rejected.
After local success, storage export/Git publication form a separate failure phase: publication failure reports successful local analysis and retains the new local release. Export precedes requested post-output cleanup so archives contain actual build bytes. A failure during this later cleanup is explicitly reported as such; there is no external publication rollback. No pre-build Git snapshot or second post-build commit is needed. Upstream selection/native credentials and publication retry identity remain separate unfinished work.
Prepared checks cover each hook/analysis failure, initially absent VERSION, exact old output/docs bytes and empty directories, renderer execution/missing promotion, exact YAML comments/render lists, restore-failure backup retention with external sentinels, and successful local analysis followed by failed storage publication. These are unrun: no local compilation under memory pressure; remote CI and independent review are still required. No power-loss atomicity, concurrent-writer or global script-side-effect guarantee is claimed. M2 attempt/release records and analysis-free retry commands remain open.
PR141 review corrections: normalize selected-input identities before comparing root containment (including Windows namespace forms); require nonempty supported document artifacts before project promotion; remove prior expected individual artifacts and project staging immediately before rendering. New regressions cover nested scripts/hooks modifying or deleting themselves, empty renderer staging, stale individual artifacts, cache purge during failed analysis, and unavailable recovery bytes without further deletion. These amendments require fresh remote CI and independent review. Project artifact scanning remains a conservative supported-document check, not a complete renderer manifest guarantee.
Further review keeps project promotion conservative: require a freshly created tree containing a nonempty supported document, rather than guessing per-input filenames from incomplete document-only format metadata. Fake PDF rendering tests cover explicit and inherited project formats. Complete expected-output manifests remain unimplemented; individual document format inference is still a separate known limitation. Selected managed script/hook paths reject symlinks along the original path before canonical identity comparison. System recovery temp anchors are canonicalized, including cache-free operations, without weakening user-path symlink rejection.
Bookdown’s framework-controlled <book_filename>_files source/destination are resolved and guarded before writes, with default _main and portable custom stems. Their exact prior bytes/presence join the recovery set. A fake successful render followed by a failing post-hook checks both default/custom native asset trees and released docs are restored. Unsupported path-like stems fail instead of traversing outside the project. Remote verification and independent review remain required.

text:

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Different/new: the audited Rust baseline scanned/hash-named files, reopened them for copy, trusted existing objects, normalized Unix literal backslashes into slashes, accepted missing/file sources as empty snapshots and treated manifest existence as verification. Literal backslash names are rejected rather than conflated with nested paths. Original source bytes are read only.
Hash the exact stream copied into temporary storage; validate existing object bytes before trusting the digest key. Immutable objects/manifests publish without clobber; manifest conflicts fail instead of truncating existing bytes. Manifest inspection parses/validates JSON and filename hash; file inspection hashes referenced objects. Index replacement uses complete staged bytes with CSV escaping for label/version. Existing empty-directory and dedup/version-sensitive manifest tests remain. Remote CI/review are pending.
This advances existing MiguelRodo/issues#688–690 rather than creating duplicate roadmap issues. Broader CAS lifecycle/GC, a consistent concurrent-source snapshot, multi-writer index updates and crash durability remain open. Failed index publication may leave a complete unindexed manifest; object residue is valid but not a successful indexed export. There is no full cross-filesystem metadata transaction or global scientific reproducibility guarantee. Existing R package remains untouched.
PR145 review adds shared manifest file/directory prefix-collision validation. Logical files a and a/b cannot coexist, independent of input order or intervening names. Both inspection strategies are tested with real digest-matching objects so the rejection proves layout validation, not an unrelated missing-object failure.
CAS metadata readers/writers require regular files before reading existing manifest or index bytes; Unix named-pipe regressions use a bounded completion check so hostile special metadata cannot block verification or ingestion indefinitely.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Different/new (approved explicit-action policy): no commit/fetch/push/token requirement is inferred from Git metadata. Omitted commits and not_behind checks are off; explicit actions use the per-run environment. Commit builds fail before writes when Git already contains changes, preserving unrelated work; staged-index no-op is success. Publish one HEAD refspec to the configured current upstream, never origin/main. Custom pushRemote/pushDefault/remote.push routing is conservatively rejected early rather than silently choosing the wrong destination. Local release success remains distinct from publication failure. The retained reference projr and legacy Rust are evidence, not authority for these newer confirmed decisions.
Native Git authentication is default. Explicit use_proj_cred_helper enables only existing single-line environment tokens on standard HTTPS github.com remotes; no build calls GitHub CLI token discovery. Fixed helper code accepts only HTTPS github.com credential requests; the token is quoted environment data, not argv or shell source. The helper list resets for that one command; no persistent config or credentials are created. Captured network failures report status without reflecting potential secret stderr. Other hosts use native configured authentication. See Git’s credential helper protocol and upstream/refspec documentation.
Ponytail full-mode review reuses native Git, existing providers and shared environment context. No new dependency or credential store. Prepared remote checks use fake Git/GH to cover zero implicit calls, configured fetch only, real upstream/refspec, no-op/single commit, dirty-input preservation, native versus opt-in helper behavior, host/protocol denial, punctuation as literal token data, helper reset and secret-free argv/diagnostics. No real network/auth action is tested. Remote CI and independent review are pending; CAS integrity and analysis-free publication retries remain open.
PR143 reviewer note: the shared Windows ASCII assignment restriction also applies to public legacy EnvGuard::track_and_set, not just file-based keys. Inherited native environment values remain preserved; the legacy mutation APIs remain outside the build-path concurrency guarantee.
PR144 review guards force untracked-file and submodule visibility during the clean check, reject pushurl and multiple effective push URLs before writes, and disable follow-tags/submodule recursion for the single explicit push. Extra destinations are also checked at dispatch. Git’s executable is resolved explicitly from the per-run PATH (git.exe on Windows), avoiding native parent-PATH fallback in both availability checks and execution. Remote fixtures cover hidden untracked content, fan-out/redirection rejection and explicit suppression flags. Fresh exact-head checks and independent re-review are required.
The same preflight also rejects mirror pushes, absent remotes, multiple tracking merge entries and effective push/fetch endpoint differences (including expanded pushInsteadOf). Destination inspection uses get-url –push –all before controlled build writes. Native Git configuration is read only; no remote/auth settings are rewritten. Fake regressions assert each unsupported case preserves VERSION and unrelated private bytes and never reaches add/commit/fetch/push.
Captured push identity includes checked-out branch, upstream remote/ref and expanded effective endpoint, without Debug exposure. Revalidate the complete supported identity immediately before commit and again before push. Hook/script changes to URL, pushurl, mirror, branch, ref or remote fail publication without redirecting the push; successful local VERSION/output are retained. Fake regressions switch those values after an analysis marker and assert no add/commit/push occurs. This guards within-run mutation, not an atomic lock against concurrent external Git changes.
The sibling public post_build_sync API now uses the same captured-context checked publication helper as build_project. A fake commit hook changing the endpoint is rejected before push. Explicit Git lookup anchors directories absolutely but preserves the candidate leaf spelling, supporting symlink-based name dispatchers; a fake git-to-dispatcher symlink regression prevents argv[0] canonicalization regressions.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Different/new: the cooperating-script-only PR123 preview guarantee is extended using reviewed exact-byte recovery from PR141. Recovery must not remove allowed cache.

Missing Unicode components reject only when overlap comparison reaches an ambiguous alias; disjoint existing/ASCII directory prefixes rule out overlap before a Unicode output leaf. title: Run your first analysis
text:
WarningTry it on a disposable project



Use sample data or a disposable copy of your project. Production builds (proj build) can modify or remove files, and safety fixes are still pending. Never run production builds on the only copy of important work. Previews are not a security sandbox; code you run can still change files.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
1. Make a small project
In an Ubuntu terminal, choose a new folder and open it:
mkdir projcli-example
cd projcli-example
Create a file named _proj.yml with this content:
directories:
  raw-data:
    path: _raw_data
  cache:
    path: _tmp
  output:
    path: _output
build:
  scripts: [analysis.py]
The paths are explicit: runtime does not supply missing mappings or invent undeclared labels.








Label
Folder
Role in this example




raw-data
_raw_data
Input files; unused because our three measurements are built into the script.


cache
_tmp
Temporary results; the script writes inside _tmp/preview.


output
_output
Result files; unused by this preview.



Only cache is used by this Python example. The other two mappings match the local initializer’s preset. No docs path is implied: document rendering needs an explicit docs mapping too.
The explicit build.scripts list selects our one script. No Git setup, remote repository or initialization command is needed for this manual setup.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
2. Add an analysis
Create analysis.py in the same folder:
import csv
import os
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import mean

root = Path(os.environ["PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT"])
preview = root / "_tmp" / "preview"
preview.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

measurements = [10, 12, 14]
result = preview / "summary.csv"
with result.open("w", newline="") as handle:
    writer = csv.writer(handle)
    writer.writerow(["count", "mean"])
    writer.writerow([len(measurements), mean(measurements)])

print(f"Saved {result}")
The three measurements are deliberately built into the script so there is no data download or extra package installation. The script uses the project root provided by projcli and explicitly writes to _tmp/preview.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
3. Check, then run
proj --project . yml read
proj --project . --non-interactive build-dev
cat _tmp/preview/summary.csv
The CSV should contain:
count,mean
3,12
The validation command reads configuration. The preview runs the script. Running it again replaces this example’s CSV; change a measurement and rerun to see the mean change.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
4. Understand what changed
The script creates _tmp/preview/summary.csv. The CLI does not create a VERSION file, publish to docs, or export an archive during this preview.
A preview is not a sandbox: your script can still write elsewhere if you tell it to. Keep preview writes in an explicit temporary folder.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
Starting another project
In another new project folder, local-only directory setup is available:
proj --project . --non-interactive init directories
When no base or active profile configuration exists, this writes _proj.yml with the explicit raw-data: _raw_data, cache: _tmp and output: _output paths, creates those folders, and updates ignore files. It does not run Git or GitHub setup. Existing configuration files are preserved; only their declared directories are created.
The generated file omits build.scripts, allowing the normal shallow script discovery. To choose an exact analysis, add a scripts list as above. An explicit scripts: [] selects no analysis scripts; hooks can still run. Initialization does not turn an absent scripts key into an empty list.

title: Project and execution behavior
text:
This is the product behavior contract. Confirmed decisions below guide implementation; they are not claims that the current CLI already implements them. Proposals require review before they become requirements. The compatibility log records pinned projr comparisons, decisions, actual test evidence, Ponytail reviews and remaining gaps; update it with each PR.



A project is one analysis/build unit anchored at a selected root directory. It has settings, version information and named resource paths where applicable. Resource paths may be outside the root; a project need not be a Git repository.
Explicit project selection overrides discovery and selects that exact directory.
Automatic discovery walks upward from the invocation directory. The nearest recognized project root wins, including when projects are nested. Discovery does not search downward for projects.
Retain existing projr root markers, including standalone VERSION and README, VCS roots, R-package/RStudio/renv/Quarto project markers, and extend recognition for pyproject.toml, Project.toml and JuliaProject.toml. Proj configuration files _proj.yml / _projr.yml also identify a root. requirements.txt and Manifest.toml alone do not. Recognition must no longer require VERSION before considering the other markers.
_proj.yml is the primary base configuration. Accept _projr.yml as a legacy alias and fail clearly if both base files exist; do not silently merge them.
Configuration precedence follows projr: local overrides profiles, profiles override base, and earlier-listed profiles win conflicts with later ones.
Missing dev.scripts falls back to build.scripts. An explicit empty list in either selects no analysis scripts and never triggers fallback/discovery. Hooks still run; production version/publication/export behavior remains available for upload-only workflows. Development previews never publish. Analysis cleanup and promotion are skipped when no analysis is selected, preserving upload inputs.
With no recognized marker, discovery falls back to cwd. This does not waive build validation: builds require an active root-level proj configuration. The agreed _proj.yml / legacy _projr.yml names apply; explicitly activated profile files may supply configuration, but inactive profile files alone do not. No-config build assumptions from the initial roadmap are superseded.
Every framework/resource directory used at runtime must be explicitly declared. Initialization may write familiar projr defaults into configuration; runtime must not synthesize missing directory mappings or unknown subpaths.
Unsupported behavior-affecting configuration fails before mutations.
Failed supported builds must restore pre-build state except permitted cache residue. This is required behavior, not an implemented transaction guarantee.
Storage/publication retries must have an upload-only route without rerunning analysis or falsely recording a new analysis. Explicit-empty analysis supports hooks/publication, but full retry identity/transaction semantics are separate.
The existing R package is entirely off limits in this effort. Direct R frontend integration is later work; no existing helper changes or parity claims follow from these Rust changes.
Default script/document enumeration is shallow at the selected project root. Subdirectory targets require explicit selection or renderer project configuration.
Native runner working-directory behavior is the default; provide an explicit project-root execution override. Rscript/Python inherit launch cwd, source() normally inherits caller cwd, and QMD/Rmd document execution has its own native defaults. Selecting a nested file does not redefine project identity.
Resolve logical role targets from captured root/config/profiles/run version. Safe output/data roles use declared versioned cache; configured final destinations are separate. Auto path representation is caller-relative ordinarily and absolute in explicitly supplied render context; explicit absolute/relative bases override.
Embedded HTML is the supported target. Default embedding only when effective settings are unspecified; preserve explicit/inherited false. Literal Markdown/ LaTeX retain native resource meaning. Linked portability is deferred.
The resolved root is captured for the run. Path helpers, including a future frontend’s projr_path_get(), resolve against that root even if a renderer or user script changes its working directory.
A supported Quarto project’s root must equal the proj root. Nested Quarto projects beneath that root are unsupported for now. Nested document files are distinct from nested Quarto projects.
QMD rendering through projr, quarto::quarto_render(), and RStudio QMD Render are a future frontend parity goal, outside the bounded Rust M1 completion gate. Evaluation-directory/root-helper parity is not currently established. R Markdown Knit is a distinct entrypoint and must be verified separately. Shared project configuration and direct-entry root resolution are required; CLI-only flags or a parent process environment cannot establish this parity.
Direct rendering does not imply the build, version, commit or archive/export side effects of a proj-managed build.
Renderer evaluation roots must use supported renderer controls. Setting only the parent process cwd is insufficient. Root identity and evaluation cwd remain separate concepts; document asset/reference resolution is not redefined here.

The project root is the analysis workspace’s top-level directory, not the user’s operating-system home directory. Resolving a named resource path is also distinct from changing cwd or selecting a new root.




Apply the base filename compatibility rule consistently to profile/local files. The effective proj profile-list source is now defined below; renderer-native profile settings are not silently rewritten.
Evaluate Quarto execute-dir and R Markdown knit_root_dir / knitr root.dir for root-relative execution. Define the shared persistent configuration and direct-entry initialization before broad renderer changes; do not add nested Quarto project support or rely only on flags passed by proj.
Frontend transport/bindings and remaining environment/YAML compatibility details must be explicit. Familiar projr directory defaults belong in init-generated configuration only; Rust’s _raw and synthesized raw/data runtime paths are not acceptable substitutes for undeclared directories.




The core root finder implements nearest-recognized-ancestor discovery without a VERSION prerequisite. Its marker tests cover the retained projr patterns and deliberate Python/Julia/proj-config extensions and cwd fallback. Builds now require active configuration and typed validation rejects unsupported fields. Explicit directory mappings are enforced without runtime path defaults; full failure restoration remains open; historical passing fixtures do not demonstrate those new requirements. Individual scripts currently start at project root; changing to native runner defaults with an explicit override is pending. Captured-root stability is implemented for core CLI child queries after cwd changes, including independent simultaneous roots; direct R frontend/renderer parity remains unimplemented. Base-file aliases and first-wins profile merging use one merged typed configuration for validation and build script/hook selection. Profile/local filenames retain their existing _projr- form for now. Explicit empty script selection now skips analysis while preserving hooks and production publication; its tests cover production archive bytes and preview nonpublication without invoking real renderers.
Verify nested projects, explicit selection, paths containing spaces, shallow default enumeration, explicit subdirectory scripts, changed cwd, and each supported renderer’s evaluation root. Compare the same nested QMD through projr, quarto::quarto_render(), and RStudio QMD Render; test R Markdown Knit separately. Reject a nested Quarto project clearly. Verify that direct rendering leaves proj-managed release/version/export state alone. Use tiny fixtures and remote CI where practical. Subprocess execution is not a security sandbox, and path hashes alone do not establish scientific correctness or a reproducible environment.



The R wrapper/CRAN design note records separate CLI installation, unconditional R-only tests, conditional CRAN executable tests and mandatory pinned/checksummed executable integration in our CI. It is future design, not a shipped wrapper, CRAN approval or automatic-download permission.



Production builds and direct cleanup helpers reject project-root/ancestor write destinations, resource/staging overlaps, selected-input containment, VCS metadata, path separators in labels and symlinked write destinations. Empty analysis still runs hooks and must validate managed destinations. Disjoint external resource paths remain supported. Generic directory moves require an existing source and disjoint destination with resolved parents; symlink aliases are rejected.
Project renderers are conservatively rejected when managed cleanup trees contain recognized source-like documents or linked entries; this is not exact renderer input discovery and can reject generated Markdown. Individual outputs must use portable leaf filenames and may not replace framework configuration/state. Concrete cache/output/asset paths are checked before VERSION or ignore writes. Literal project roots are escaped for explicit include/exclude globs so brackets in a root cannot hide selected inputs from safety checks.
These checks do not establish atomic promotion, full rollback, protection against concurrent filesystem replacement, or undo arbitrary external script effects.



The pinned legacy audit records unresolved safety and correctness findings and the regression evidence required before claiming fixes.

Builds resolve one environment snapshot and pass it to their child commands and configuration-profile selection. Environment files do not mutate the parent process on this path. Inherited OS values win over local, earlier environment profiles and base assignments; explicit build profiles override inherited PROJR_PROFILE. The same values reach dependency probes, scripts/hooks/renderers and existing Git helpers. Direct public legacy EnvGuard APIs and CLI startup guards still mutate process state and are not concurrent environment APIs. This change does not approve credential injection policy or establish a sanitized/sandboxed environment.



Script and hook subprocesses inherit invocation cwd by default, retaining explicit selected input paths. Quarto and individual R Markdown retain native execution directory settings. Explicit --execution-dir project passes the captured root via supported renderer controls. Input/mode/root remain data arguments to fixed R code. This does not imply direct R/IDE parity or a changed resource URL policy. The existing R package remains untouched.
Nested Quarto project metadata is rejected for selected documents and conservatively scanned implicit source trees. Individual rendering models one document-local format: HTML, PDF, Word, or supported native presentation/EPUB variants. Unknown/multiple formats, inherited individual metadata, custom R Markdown output filenames, dynamic R Markdown runtime and document-rendering hooks fail before controlled writes. Project-render validation remains conservative fresh-tree validation, not a complete renderer output manifest. Unsupported layout rejection does not assert renderer parity.
clear_output accepts only pre, post, or never; directory ignore accepts all, git, rbuild (case-insensitive), or an empty list. Invalid values fail before analysis, ignore synchronization or cleanup, including direct cleanup APIs.



Ingestion requires an existing directory, disjoint from its CAS storage and project index. Reject linked/unsupported source entries, non-UTF-8 filenames and ambiguous logical paths; logical identities use slash-separated components and case-sensitive names. Digests are canonical 64-character lowercase hexadecimal BLAKE3 values. Copy and hash the same stream; verify existing objects before reuse. Publish complete objects/manifests without replacing conflicting content. Replace project index bytes through a same-directory temporary file, escaping CSV metadata fields.
Manifest inspection validates structure and manifest byte identity; file inspection also hashes referenced object bytes. This does not provide a stable snapshot across concurrent source changes, multi-writer serialization, power-loss durability or one transaction across remote manifest and project index. Failure may leave valid orphan objects or an unindexed complete manifest; errors propagate and old index bytes stay intact. No source file is modified by ingestion. Symlink-alias paths remain unsupported under the conservative path guards; callers should supply resolved physical paths.



Git commits, pushes and network/upstream checks default off even when Git metadata exists. Only the resolved configured actions execute. Commit-enabled builds require clean initial Git state to avoid sweeping in unrelated edits; no-op commits succeed. Push captures the current branch’s configured upstream remote/reference before build writes. Missing upstream and unmodeled custom push-only routing fail early. Native authentication is the default. An explicit token-helper opt-in uses fixed host-scoped code and ephemeral environment data, never secret argv/source or persistent credentials. Local build success remains distinct from publication failure.



Preview captures managed root files/config/VERSION, selected inputs, declared output/docs trees, configured local publication stores and ordinary VCS metadata. Restore exact captured bytes/presence on both success and failure; restoration failure makes preview fail and reports retained recovery data when available. Declared cache is disposable and excluded from recovery; preview/cache artifacts remain there. No Git/publication operations execute in preview.
Recovery uses private temporary storage outside project cache. Unsafe linked or overlapping recovery paths fail before analysis; file-based/worktree VCS pointers are unsupported for this bounded metadata guarantee. This does not redirect arbitrary script writes, protect undeclared/external effects, prevent concurrent reads of temporary modifications, or provide sandbox/crash/concurrent-writer atomicity. New unmanaged files are not a whole-project snapshot. Automatic preview output isolation remains separate from post-run captured-state preservation.



Release/install plumbing must verify version-bound platform assets/checksums before replacement and use locked remote tests/builds. The pipeline creates a draft prerelease only; publication and user-local WSL binary installation follow explicit artifact verification. See delivery boundaries. No local source compilation or production-readiness claim follows from installer CI.



Opt-in --machine emits protocol-v1 results/errors on stdout, with capability version negotiation independent of project discovery. Static error codes avoid reflecting credentials/config/argv. Queries return typed values; other existing commands reuse the CLI through a noninteractive worker whose logs use stderr. See machine interface for supported shapes and limits. This is a transport boundary over existing anyhow errors, not a second domain-error overhaul.



One effective profile list is selected before config/environment reads: CLI, nonempty PROJR_PROFILE, nonempty QUARTO_PROFILE fallback, then base/local build.profile default. Earlier profiles still win; local config is highest. A profile’s own build.profile does not redirect an already selected run. Native QUARTO_PROFILE rendering settings remain distinct; no R helper bridge follows. The private per-run PROJ_RUN_CONTEXT snapshot carries only root, effective profiles, validated final directory mappings, active version and mode. Child path/version queries consume it after cwd/YAML/VERSION changes; explicit other-project selection discards it. Missing/invalid context fails clearly rather than rediscovering a root.
Preview retains an existing dev version, or uses dev1 from a release, without changing VERSION. Production uses the requested incremented release version from before hooks through rendering; success leaves dev1 of that release for subsequent development, and failure restores original bytes. Cache keys use v1.2.3-4 spelling; legacy version text APIs/files retain their accepted dotted representation. Final directory lookup remains unchanged in this slice; safe logical routing, render-context representation and native execution/embedding are subsequent work. Old-version renderer staging remains a known gap until the routing slice.



Safe output/data/docs-class lookup uses the selected eligible cache-class mapping, the captured active version and exact configured label. Final lookup preserves the physical mapping, including external paths. No implicit data directory is invented: a data-class label must be declared. Directory insertion order is retained through configuration merging and the child snapshot. File fragments are relative and cannot replace/escape the role root. Queries never create directories. The initial explicit safe/final CLI slice keeps final as its transitional default; safe-by-default behavior must land together with production output consumers. Preview artifacts written through explicit safe lookup remain inspectable in cache.


Within directories, one cache-class mapping with boolean safe: true selects the safe cache. Otherwise an eligible exact cache label wins, then the first eligible cache-class mapping in merged declaration order. safe: false excludes a candidate. Overrides retain existing key positions. Multiple explicit selections, non-boolean flags, flags on non-cache roles, or all declared caches excluded are validation errors before build mutations. A genuinely cache-free operation remains valid without any cache mapping. The effective selected label is frozen with the run context; children do not recompute it from subsequently changed YAML.
Legacy R data is package-generated output, not a generic input role. Its replacement/legacy normalization belongs to the separate output-r-data slice; this cache-selection change does not silently rename existing mappings.




Auto/absolute/relative are independent of safe/final target and execution cwd. Known managed renderer children receive an explicit bounded descriptor; no suffix or cwd-marker heuristics. Ordinary auto is caller-relative at query time; renderer auto is absolute. Relative bases are caller/project/known document/absolute custom directory. Explicit relative is strict across roots/drives; auto may fall back to absolute. Project renders without a single document reject document-relative base. The intermediate CLI retains absolute/final defaults until consumers switch. Existing R helper/direct IDE parity remains unimplemented and outside Rust M1.
Native execution policy (supersedes earlier unconditional root-cwd wording): build and build-dev default to --execution-dir native. Plain scripts/hooks inherit the invocation cwd, not each source file’s parent; R source() normally inherits its caller cwd. Individual Rmd rendering leaves knit_root_dir unset and Quarto receives no execution-dir override, preserving native document/project settings. --execution-dir project explicitly requests captured-root execution for scripts/hooks, Quarto and individual Rmd. Project render drivers run from the selected project root to select the project, independently of chunk cwd. Project-wide Bookdown root override is currently rejected early because its render_site entrypoint does not expose the individual knit-root argument. Captured project/profile/version and logical path identity do not change with execution cwd. No existing R helper bridge or literal Markdown resource rewriting is implied.



This source slice wires output consumers to the captured active version and selected eligible cache; the CLI lookup defaults remain transitional final/absolute until the following defaults slice. settings is runtime policy, build selects actions, and parameters remain analytical data. settings.output-clear-stage is none (default), pre or post. Explicit --output-clear-stage wins over merged settings, then legacy build.clear_output YAML, then PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT, then none. Legacy environment/build never means none. Canonical settings uses none only; invalid values, explicit null and unsupported settings fail in their source layer. This deliberately changes R’s production fallback pre; R has no settings section.
After read-only validation/recovery setup, start hooks run first. Other preparation (ignore metadata, renderer staging and fresh native artifact isolation) follows. Pre-clear is immediately before analysis; post-clear is immediately after successful analysis, before restoration/staging/promotion/hooks. These clear configured final output/data roots, never the versioned cache and never preview final destinations. Output actions disabled by output_run:false also skip final-output clearing. An empty analysis selection remains upload-only and skips analysis-related clearing. Docs finalization is a separate fresh-document operation, not ordinary output clearing.
Fresh renderer artifacts are copied to selected-cache/projr/v/docs in previews and releases. Individual render source location is preserved for native resource semantics. Versioned cache files remain inspectable; failed renderer scratch is retained there too. mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
installer="$(mktemp)"
curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/bbd12edc8de9865a96b6145d0c7702f1300cb1a8/install-local.sh" -o "$installer" &&

hash -r

title: Configuration _proj.yml
text:
The _proj.yml file dictates the structural map of your project. It configures the foundational paths and mapping logic used by the CLI.


Custom directory labels are strictly validated against a set of foundational prefixes: - cache - raw - data - output - docs
These prefixes are case-insensitive. Any label defined in the configuration must begin with one of these approved identifiers.



Every declared directory needs a nonempty path. Runtime does not insert missing cache/raw/output/data/docs mappings or synthesize subpaths for undeclared labels. For example, declaring raw-data: {path: _raw_data} makes raw-data available; it does not create an undeclared raw or raw-data-extra resource. ASCII case is ignored and case-only duplicate labels are rejected.
proj --project . --non-interactive init directories creates a missing _proj.yml once with explicit raw-data: _raw_data, cache: _tmp, and output: _output paths. It preserves existing base/profile files, creates only declared resource directories, and does not invoke Git/GitHub or add an R code directory. The preset omits build.scripts, preserving shallow discovery; it never serializes an accidental empty analysis list. To render documents, declare a docs mapping too.
Production state and project-render staging require a declared cache directory. Framework version/staging children are derived inside that declared cache; this is distinct from inventing undeclared resource labels. Storage content labels must be declared and relative storage paths use the captured project root.



Each cache-class directory may include boolean safe. One explicit safe: true selects that cache; otherwise an eligible exact cache label wins, then the first eligible cache in merged declaration order. safe: false excludes a candidate. Profile/local overrides retain existing declaration positions. For example:
directories:
  cache:
    path: _tmp
  cache-analysis:
    path: _analysis_cache
    safe: true
This selects _analysis_cache for explicit safe logical output lookup. Multiple true selections, non-boolean values (including null), selection flags on non-cache roles, and all declared cache candidates excluded are validation errors. Each layer’s explicit values are checked before merging; null cannot inherit a previous boolean. Cache-free queries and operations that do not consume a cache remain valid. The chosen safe cache is frozen in child run context. Existing cleanup and project-render consumers still require literal cache in this transitional slice; their integration follows separately before the safe default is enabled.



The system performs strict validation on _proj.yml: - If a defined directory label uses an unsupported prefix layout, a validation error string will be returned and execution will fail. - All references must resolve correctly; otherwise, the CLI will output an error detailing the structurally invalid labels or malformed content.



The _proj.yml file supports a top-level config block for project-wide settings:

config.git.engine: The Git execution engine to use. Can be auto (default) or system. This determines how the CLI interfaces with Git capabilities natively.
config.git.use_proj_cred_helper: Defaults to false: use existing native Git authentication. Explicit true permits an existing single-line GITHUB_PAT, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN for standard HTTPS github.com remotes through a temporary host-scoped helper. There is no automatic token discovery or GitHub CLI call during builds. Tokens are environment data, never argv or shell source; persistent auth settings are unchanged.




The _proj.yml file supports a top-level parameters block for arbitrary nested parameter evaluation. This allows you to define custom metadata and deeply queried values throughout your execution environment.
The configuration engine also supports several aliases for this block: parameter, params, and param. However, multiple alias conflicts within the same configuration file are structurally rejected during validation to prevent mapping confusion.



The _proj.yml file supports a top-level remotes block, which currently supports a local mapping of standalone storage vaults.

local: A mapping where keys represent remote titles and values configure the vault:

path: The physical absolute or relative path to the remote storage directory.
structure: Specifies the storage structure algorithm. Must be cas (Content-Addressable Storage).
content: An array of string tags (matching foundational prefixes or defined directories) specifying which project output directories to sync into the remote upon build completion.
inspect: manifest validates JSON, logical paths/digests and manifest filename/content identity; file additionally hashes every referenced object and compares actual bytes. Manifest-only inspection does not verify object bytes.





The _proj.yml file can also contain a build block to configure the behavior of the proj build and proj build-dev execution engine. The build block supports the following sub-keys:

dest: An optional list of remote target strings. These targets must be mapped to explicit configurations within the remotes.local block. During post-build execution, resolved content directories matching these tags are piped to the CAS engine for deduplicated storage synchronization.
scripts: An optional list of explicit script paths or glob patterns to execute during the build pipeline.

Globbing patterns are supported.
Prefix a pattern with ! to exclude matching files from execution.
When provided, this selects scripts instead of automatic discovery. Document targets may be grouped for rendering, so mixed script and document targets are not guaranteed to run in the exact listed order.

hooks: An optional map of lifecycle hook scripts to execute.

pre: Scripts executed before the actual build phase.
post: Scripts executed after analysis/promotion, before VERSION and publication.
both: Scripts executed during both pre and post phases.

profile: An optional environment profile identifier. When set, the system injects the PROJR_PROFILE environment variable into the isolated subprocess for all executed scripts and project rendering commands. This can be overridden at runtime via the --profile CLI flag.
git: An optional Git integration configuration. This can be a boolean toggle or an object mapping out detailed toggles:

commit: Defaults to false, including inside an existing Git repository. Explicit true requires initially clean Git state and commits once after successful local build; an unchanged staged index is a successful no-op.
push: Defaults to false. Explicit true publishes HEAD to the current branch’s configured upstream remote/reference. Missing upstream or custom push-only routing fails before build writes; origin/main is never invented.

restrictions: Configuration block to enforce Git checks specifically during production builds:

only_branches: A list of allowed branch names. Production builds will abort if the current branch is not in this list.
not_branches: A list of restricted branch names. Production builds will abort if the current branch is in this list.
not_behind: Omitted/false performs no fetch. Explicit true fetches the current configured upstream and compares its state. If enabled, production builds will verify that the local branch has an upstream tracking remote and is not behind it, aborting if the local branch needs to pull upstream changes.

clear_output: An optional string controlling workspace clearing routines for output directories. Can be set to "pre", "post", or "never". If omitted, defaults to evaluating the PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT environment variable.




You can define a dev block to completely override specific configurations during development builds (proj build-dev).

scripts: A list of script paths or globs. During development builds, this array entirely overrides build.scripts. An explicitly empty array ([]) selects no analysis scripts. An absent dev.scripts inherits build.scripts. Hooks can still run.
hooks: A mapping identical to build.hooks. When specified, these completely replace build.hooks during a development build.
old_dev_remove: Retained configuration field. The current preview protections skip CLI cleanup of prior caches during development builds, even when this is true. Scripts and hooks still control their own writes.





PROJR_AUTO_INSTALL: During the proj build pre-flight checks, if required R packages (like bookdown or rmarkdown) are missing, this environment variable controls remediation. If set to true, packages are automatically installed. If absent or set to false, the tool defaults to an interactive terminal prompt (if available) or fails hard.




build declares actions; settings controls how they run. Parameters are analysis inputs, not execution controls. This is an intentional extension beyond projr.
settings:
  output-clear-stage: none
Use none to preserve other existing final files, pre to clear immediately before analysis, or post to clear immediately after successful analysis and before output promotion/finalization. Preview never clears released outputs. Pre-hooks run before pre-clear; end hooks run after finalization immediately before the next-dev bump. The command’s explicit –output-clear-stage overrides merged settings; those override legacy build.clear_output, then PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT, then the new none default. Legacy never is accepted in the legacy field/environment. The canonical settings key accepts only none/pre/post, with invalid values/null rejected before merge or mutation. Docs output handling remains separate. Safe/auto CLI defaults and the R-data built-in are following focused slices, not delivered merely by adding settings here.

The build pipeline script execution engine for the project.
This command evaluates what files need to be run based on configuration layout parameters (build.scripts in _proj.yml) or filesystem auto-discovery. Production Build Restrictions: Checks if branch rules (only_branches, not_branches) or upstream synchronicity (not_behind) are violated during a production build run.
Remote Export Pipeline: During the post-build phase, conditionally exports resolved local target outputs into a deduplicated Content-Addressable Storage (CAS) vault as defined via build.dest targets in remotes.local.
System Git Provider Abstracted: Git mutations safely resolve through a strictly encapsulated host System Git adapter, securely avoiding hanging inputs and ensuring older systems correctly push mutations.
Mutual Exclusion Checking: Before executing, proj build checks for project-level configurations (_quarto.yml and _bookdown.yml). If both exist and the build targets include Quarto or RMarkdown documents, it throws an error to prevent conflicting rendering.
Explicit Execution (Path A):

Define exact scripts, exclusions (starting with !), or sub-directory globs in _proj.yml under build.scripts.
Can rewrite _quarto.yml or _bookdown.yml configuration if specific subset documents are requested.
Maintains order relative to Python and R scripts, while correctly clustering and executing project documents together.

Fallback Execution (Path B):

If no build.scripts is provided, the engine auto-discovers build targets.
Will execute a Quarto project if _quarto.yml exists, or a Bookdown project if _bookdown.yml exists.
Otherwise, it falls back to a shallow workspace sweep and runs .qmd, .Rmd, .R, and .py files in that strict order.

title: proj build
text: Every resolved file or project rendering task runs inside its own completely independent subprocess, isolated via environment profiles (PROJR_PROFILE) and correct working directory assignments (current_dir), preventing memory leaks and state pollution across execution runs.

title: proj build
text:
proj build-dev
Development runs execute the existing script selection with development Git settings disabled. The CLI does not create or update VERSION, update ignore files, clear released output or previous caches, promote rendered documents into docs, or export to configured local archives. These rules apply on success and failure, even when production configuration enables cleanup, commits or export.
Scripts should explicitly write preview artefacts into their declared cache or staging locations. A subprocess is not a filesystem sandbox: scripts, hooks and renderers can still write where their own code/configuration directs them. Renderer configuration rewriting and script working-directory behavior retain their existing semantics. This change does not introduce automatic output redirection, recursive discovery or a new project-root policy.

title: proj build
text:
build.scripts: [] selects no analysis scripts. Hooks still run, and production builds can version and export existing artefacts as an upload-only workflow. Analysis cleanup, renderer setup and document promotion are skipped so those existing artefacts are preserved. The CLI does not discover scripts instead.
For previews, an absent dev.scripts inherits build.scripts; dev.scripts: [] overrides it with no analysis. Hooks still run, but previews never publish.

title: proj build
text:
Builds require root-level _proj.yml, legacy _projr.yml, or an explicitly activated _projr-<profile>.yml. Inactive profiles and _projr-local.yml alone do not qualify. Both base filenames together are an error. Unsupported control fields fail before build writes; arbitrary parameters and metadata maps are allowed. Configuration errors include their causes on stderr and return failure.
This validation is separate from project discovery. A root marker or cwd fallback does not make an unconfigured project buildable. Explicit directory enforcement, per-run environment isolation and complete managed-state failure restoration remain under development; see the behavior contract and pinned legacy audit.
Explicit script/hook include patterns must match at least one file. Use an empty list (scripts: []) when intentionally selecting no analysis; unmatched configured includes return an error instead of a successful no-op.
Native execution policy (supersedes earlier unconditional root-cwd wording): build and build-dev default to --execution-dir native. Plain scripts/hooks inherit the invocation cwd, not each source file’s parent; R source() normally inherits its caller cwd. Individual Rmd rendering leaves knit_root_dir unset and Quarto receives no execution-dir override, preserving native document/project settings. --execution-dir project explicitly requests captured-root execution for scripts/hooks, Quarto and individual Rmd. Project render drivers run from the selected project root to select the project, independently of chunk cwd. Project-wide Bookdown root override is currently rejected early because its render_site entrypoint does not expose the individual knit-root argument. Captured project/profile/version and logical path identity do not change with execution cwd. No existing R helper bridge or literal Markdown resource rewriting is implied.

title: Command exit status
text:
Successful CLI commands return exit status zero. Reported operation failures return a nonzero status and a diagnostic on stderr, including configuration/path queries, version reads/writes, ignore updates and initialization. Argument parsing errors also return nonzero.
For example, a malformed _proj.yml makes proj yml read --project demo fail, so a shell or frontend can stop instead of treating the diagnostic as success. Failed Git staging, commits and GitHub creation propagate as initialization errors; a failed remote inspection does not proceed to GitHub creation.
This defines success versus failure, not stable error codes, a JSON result schema or a capability protocol. Diagnostics remain human-readable text. Commands may perform work before failing; a nonzero status is not a rollback guarantee.


proj build-dev --project demo --non-interactive
--non-interactive disables the CLI’s own prompts and automatic R-package installation, including when PROJR_AUTO_INSTALL=true. Missing dependencies produce an error. Script, hook and renderer runners and controlled R dependency probes receive closed stdin. The mode is inherited by managed children as PROJ_NON_INTERACTIVE=true.
Initialization still performs requested operations using its existing defaults. This flag does not choose project markers, change configuration precedence or define a structured result protocol. Third-party code remains responsible for its own behavior after receiving EOF.

title: proj yml read
text:
Load and validate configuration without modifying the project:
proj yml read [--project <PATH>]
The command prints a validation confirmation on success and reports configuration errors on stderr. It does not dump configuration values; use proj path get to query a resolved directory path.


The base is _proj.yml, or the legacy alias _projr.yml. Having both is an error. Active _projr-<profile>.yml files override the base, with earlier-listed profiles winning conflicts. _projr-local.yml overrides all active profiles. Explicit profile selection replaces the environment list. Profile/local filename aliases are separate from the implemented base alias.
Read-only queries accept missing configuration as an empty directory inventory. Builds require an active base or explicitly activated profile at the root. Inactive profiles and local overrides alone do not qualify. Every declared directory requires an explicit nonempty path; missing labels are never invented. Unsupported control fields fail validation; metadata and parameters remain arbitrary maps. Parameter aliases normalize before merging; conflicting aliases within one file are rejected. No query writes defaults into configuration.

It creates declared directories and synchronizes ignore rules without Git/GitHub setup. Existing configuration bytes are preserved. It leaves scripts absent, preserving discovery; scripts: [] continues to mean no analysis.
Configuration validation and path queries do not change .gitignore, .Rbuildignore, configuration files, or project directories. Production builds and directory initialization request ignore synchronization explicitly. Directory initialization stops on configuration read/validation errors before changing ignore rules or creating directories.

title: Machine interface
text:
Machine interface
Use proj --machine <command> for automation. Human command output remains the default. proj capabilities (also with --machine) reports protocol/capability versions and supported command families without loading a project.
Protocol version 1 writes one JSON object and a newline to stdout. Both success and failure include protocol_version, cli_version, ok, result, and error. result is null on failure; error is null on success. Failures exit nonzero. Broken output pipes cannot receive a complete object and also exit nonzero.
proj --machine capabilities
proj --machine --project . path get --label output
proj --machine --project . version get
proj --machine --project . yml read
proj --machine --project . build-dev
Successful queries return { "path": "..." }, { "version": { "major": 1, "minor": 2, "patch": 3, "dev": 0 }, "text": "v1.2.3" }, or { "validated": true }. Configuration queries validate without returning raw configuration or parameter values. Other existing command families reuse the ordinary CLI in a noninteractive subprocess and return { "completed": true } only when that command succeeds. Unsupported command arguments fail; capability flags explicitly report absent preview isolation, attempt/release records and direct R/IDE parity.
Stable error codes are invalid_arguments, project_selection_failed, query_failed, command_failed, and worker_unavailable. Messages are static; raw config, environment values, command arguments and chained domain errors are not copied into protocol errors. This transport reuses existing anyhow domain handling tracked by issue87; it does not promise a finer domain-error taxonomy. With --machine, help/version display requests return capability negotiation.
All command progress and child stdout/stderr go to stderr, streamed directly without accumulating logs in memory. Machine mode closes child stdin and enables noninteractive policy. Child logs are user/third-party output and are not a secret redaction service; avoid printing credentials in scripts. No environment/config dump is included in the machine result. Callers must keep stdout and stderr separate.
A failed publication can follow successful local analysis. command_failed is not a rollback or retry instruction: inspect local state/diagnostics before retrying. No analysis-free publication retry or successful release record is invented here.
